findings.title: An Electron build from master cannot host against the deployed signalling service, and nothing a candidate builder reads says so
findings.claim: After this merge, the Electron page makes the service calls itself, so every request now carries an Origin (`null`, or `file://` on the socket). The deployed service predates Task 8. It refuses `Origin: file://`, and for `Origin: null` it calls `response.headers.set` on the immutable Durable Object responses for socket, checkpoint and turn. Either way an Electron candidate built from master cannot open a room socket, fetch TURN credentials or read checkpoints until the service is redeployed. The plan records only that Task 8 'ships only at Web-iii's deploy'. That reads as if Electron online play from master stays broken until Web-iii. `docs/gates.md` has no Web-i entry or warning at all.
findings.evidence: services/signalling/src/index.ts:L62 (file:// allowed only in the new code) and L74-79 (copy before setting headers, new); diff L5002 and L5015 (master: `allowed` without file://, and headers set directly on `response`); plan L36 (D-2 'ships only at Web-iii's deploy'); plan L3702 (DO stub responses have immutable headers; only `POST /v2/rooms` got CORS headers before, because Electron main sent no Origin); docs/gates.md L811 and L850-877 (the candidate and redeploy procedure, with no Web-i note; a grep for 'web-i' in gates.md finds nothing); services/signalling/README.md diff L4942-4947 (covers only `npm run dev` origins).
findings.why: The owner builds tester installers from master for playtests. Earlier milestones went out with 'service needs no redeploy', and Web-i changes no SIM_VERSION, so the natural assumption is again no redeploy. Hosting, joining, rehost and reconnect would then all fail in ordinary use on the first playtest build after this merge. That is the release-blocker class the brief names.
findings.fix: Keep master's Electron build working by deploying the Task 8 service change ahead of Web-iii. It is backward compatible: older Electron builds call from main with no Origin, so the new copy and Expose-Headers branch never runs for them, and `null`/`file://` need no `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` change. Reword D-2 at plan L36 to match. Whether or not you deploy early, add a Web-i entry to docs/gates.md saying that an Electron candidate built at or after 31c498d8 needs a signalling service deployed from that revision or later, and that the deployed service must be redeployed before any tester installer is built.

findings.title: No check starts the module host Worker from a packaged (asar) build
findings.claim: The Worker is built as `new Worker(new URL('../../worker/authorityWorker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` and loads from `out/renderer/assets/authorityWorker.js`. A packaged build loads it from inside app.asar over file://. Every Web-i gate, including `test:worker-boot` (which closed D-6), runs the unpackaged `out/`. A tester installer is the first time a module Worker would be fetched from inside an asar archive.
findings.evidence: src/network/host/workerHost.ts:L33-35; electron.vite.config.ts:L28; package.json diff L235 (`test:worker-boot` = `electron-vite build && electron scripts/network/worker-boot.cjs`, unpackaged); plan L39 (D-6 decided on the unpackaged boot); plan L56 (gate list, no packaged run).
findings.why: Hosting needs the Worker. If it fails to load from asar, every packaged host fails at `ready-timeout`, while every gate still passes.
findings.fix: Before the next installer, run the worker-boot check, or one host-runtime or duel-app pass, against `npm run package:candidate` output (win-unpacked with app.asar), and record the result in the plan ledger. If it fails, unpack the Worker chunk through `asarUnpack`.

findings.title: The duel host's leave→idle assertion was dropped without a recorded deviation
findings.claim: On master the duel gate ended with both seats leaving through the menu and reaching idle. The host now closes its window for the close gate, so only the guest's duel leave→idle is still asserted. D-9 covers only `stale`, and the plan has no entry for this.
findings.evidence: diff L401-402 (removed: `for (const app of [g, h]) { await app.request('click', { id: 'leave' }); } await phase(h, 'idle'); await phase(g, 'idle');`); scripts/network/duel-app-smoke.ts (diff L418-422: guest leave only); a grep of the plan for 'leave…idle' finds no match. Partial cover elsewhere: scripts/network/online-app-smoke.ts:L168 (sector host leave→idle) and online-recovery-smoke 'leave-old-host' (diff L2671).
findings.why: The duel is the menu's Multiplayer. Its renderer-side leave (onlineDuel's `leave: () => actions.leave()` in src/renderer/src/main.ts:L111) is not the sector's, so a regression in the host's duel leave would pass every gate.
findings.fix: Add a host duel leave→idle step that does not conflict with the close gate (for example, host a second duel lobby after the guest leaves and leave it from the host). Or record the gap as a stated deviation next to D-9.

findings.title: No test covers the clock-jump path's un-awaited suspend() then resume() on an active host
findings.claim: `createClockJumpLifecycle` fires suspend and resume synchronously, back to back (lifecycle.ts:L37). By trace the owner handles this safely: suspend's synchronous `savedState` retires the game, resume's second `savedState` only chains `gameRetiring`, and exactly one `reconnect` follows. The Worker host's own suspend listener sees `stopping` and goes to `stop('system-suspend')`, as on master. Every existing test awaits suspend before calling resume, though, so none covers this ordering.
findings.evidence: src/network/online/lifecycle.ts:L37; src/renderer/src/app/online/pageSession.ts:L96-97 (`void owner.suspend()` / `void owner.resume()`); src/network/online/onlineSession.ts:L573-581; src/network/host/workerHost.ts:L263-270; tests/onlineRecovery.test.ts:L71, L79, L250 (all `await p.owner.suspend(); await p.owner.resume()`); tests/onlineLifecycle.test.ts:L14-19 (trigger only).
findings.why: Web-ii's browser path relies on this ordering. A future change to suspend's synchronous prefix could cause a double reconnect or a stale-host race, and no test would catch it.
findings.fix: In tests/onlineRecovery.test.ts, add a case on an active hosted run that calls `void owner.suspend(); void owner.resume();` without awaiting. Assert that `invalidateLease` was called with 'suspended' then 'resumed', that the old host was disposed once, and that exactly one reconnect was dispatched.

verified: Session move preserves behaviour (diff L6364-6541, L6022-6363). onlineSession, onlinePeers, onlineDuel, onlineSector, onlineMirrors and onlineIce differ from their src/main/network originals only by import paths, MessagePortMain→MessagePort, and the stated replacements: sha256Hex for createHash, bytesToBase64/base64ToBytes/bytesEqual for Buffer, randomHex for randomBytes. onlineModes and onlineRetry are 100% renames. The only new behaviour is `releaseForUnload` (onlineSession.ts:L583-587).

mirrorStore keeps magic FTLNMIR1, the 557,056-byte cap and the 16,384-byte header cap, now over OnlineRecordStore (diff L6055-6110). seatStore keeps the 8,192-byte cap (seatStore.ts:L14). recordStore uses database 'ftlite', version 1, store 'records', keys seat-v1 and mirror-v1, one put per readwrite transaction (recordStore.ts:L9-L53).

workerHost implements HostProcessHandle unchanged (diff L5709-5969). Readiness is workerReady plus bridgeReady from transport-ready (workerHost.ts:L115-117, L236-241). The lease is invalidated on suspend and resume (L263-270, D-4). kill is idempotent through `exited || killed` (L57). The 5 s ready, request and lease paths are identical to hostProcess.ts.

Clock-jump detector: a 1 s interval and the rule `(Δwall − Δmono) > 15000` (lifecycle.ts:L5, L33-38). bfcache pagehide/pageshow with persisted:true suspends and resumes (L39-40). No visibilitychange listener exists (tests/onlineLifecycle.test.ts:L20-22). Electron uses createElectronLifecycle over the preload's app:suspend/app:resume (pageSession.ts:L50; main/index.ts:L44-46).

A non-persisted pagehide calls releaseForUnload (pageSession.ts:L98-99, L133). That calls `stop(undefined, true)`, which issues host-release before cleanup closes the socket and captures no checkpoint (onlineSession.ts:L123-129). If main's 3 s cap fires first, the later pagehide still sends the release.

Close handshake (appExit.ts:L7-37): a 3000 ms timer, an early finish on render-process-gone, one request per close or quit (a second close is preventDefault'ed and joins), a request-number-matched answer only from the main frame, and `ready` set before win.close()/app.quit() so the second close passes through. `will-prevent-unload` is preventDefault'ed, which allows unload (main/index.ts:L49). The preload answers even with no handler (preload/index.ts:L20-24). tests/appExit.test.ts covers the double close, the timeout and render-process-gone.

Trust boundary: the session object stays inside createPageOnline. The only window property is `__ftliteOnlineTest`, a frozen, non-writable, non-configurable facade without the seat token, set only when `testProbe && !packaged` (pageSession.ts:L53, L136-138). toPageOnlineConfig sets the test fields only when unpackaged, and validatePageOnlineConfig rejects packaged configs carrying them (shared/onlineConfig.ts:L30-37, L48). The preload freezes the config and falls back to disabled (preload/index.ts:L11-17). Main answers the config only to its own main frame (main/index.ts:L32-33, L40).

Signalling: `file://` is allowed like `null` (index.ts:L62). On every allowed response with an Origin, the response is copied (101 with webSocket handled) before Allow-Origin, Vary and Expose-Headers: X-FTL-Checkpoint are set (L72-79). tests/origins.test.ts covers checkpoint GET exposure for a listed origin and null, and socket 403/101 for evil, listed, null and file://.

Hidden-tab warning: active only when `bridge && !window.ftlite`, so off in Electron, and keyed on role === 'host', so off in Single player (main.ts:L88; hostVisibility.ts:L16). The lease relay path is timer-free across coordinator, serviceClient and workerHost (tests/leaseRelayEvents.test.ts).

Merge of master: main.ts wires SOLO_SHIPS, soloShip, the Valkyrn laser fit and installCrt through createPageOnline and createOnlineBridge (main.ts:L71-L136). A grep across src, tests, scripts and build finds no import of any deleted module (main/network/*, utility/authorityHost, networkTransport); only build-output.test.ts asserts their absence.

Gate rewrites reviewed: online-app-report and online-recovery-report rename utility/window counters to worker/page counters with the same equalities, and unobserved counters now stay null. stale fails by name under D-9 (diff L2601). The duel gate adds the minimized-host (≥59 Hz, lease kept) and close-gate (fresh checkpoint ≤3 s, workers===workerExits, ports 0, exit 0) assertions, both required (diff L369-L443).
